technical_and_design_decisions: Language & Ecosystem: Implementation will be in Go, matching the existing `hyperledger/fabric-config` codebase.
Unsigned ConfigUpdate Envelope: API methods generating config updates will support an optional or distinct path returning `*common.ConfigUpdateEnvelope` without requiring signing identities upfront.
Consenter Matching Rule: Consenter removal will strictly match all 4 target fields (`host`, `port`, `client_tls_cert`, and `server_tls_cert`) to prevent unintended deletions.
MSP Setters Mutability: MSP fine-grained setters will directly mutate the underlying `ConfigGroup` structure rather than relying on full copy/clone semantics via `GetMSP`/`SetMSP`.

CLI Architecture: The CLI tool for bulk operations will use standard Go CLI frameworks (e.g., Cobra/Viper), consuming Fabric SDK Go components for Peer Discovery Service integration and Orderer transaction submission.
assumptions: The environment includes access to a running Hyperledger Fabric peer/orderer instance or mock framework for integration testing.
Fabric Connection Profile specification version 2.0 is supported by the underlying client libraries used in the CLI.
All required crypto library primitives for X.509 certificate parsing and validation are available in standard Go or Fabric dependencies.

activities.activity_description: Design fine-grained Go API extensions for configtx library (U1-U5, U7-U8) and architecture for the bulk operations CLI tool (U6) including network discovery and payload signing interfaces.
Implement AddConsortium (U1), unsigned ConfigUpdate envelope generation (U2), RemoveLegacyOrdererAddresses (U3), RemoveKafkaBrokers (U4), and EtcdRaft consenter add/remove functions (U5).

Implement individual field update methods for OrdererGroup (BatchSize, BatchTimeout, MaxChannels, ConsensusType, ConsensusState, EtcdRaft metadata) (U7) and MSP setters across OrdererOrgGroup, ApplicationOrgGroup, and ConsortiumOrgGroup (U8).

Implement CLI tool supporting batchUpdate.json parsing, connection profile integration, discovery service config fetching, dry-run mode, stacked operation execution, identity signing, and orderer submission (U6).
Update code examples demonstrating new APIs (consortium additions, Kafka to EtcdRaft migration guide, orderer field setters, and MSP field setters) (U1, U4, U7, U8).

Develop comprehensive unit tests for library API additions, end-to-end integration tests for CLI bulk operations across multiple channels, dry-run output validations, and certificate validation checks.
